articles.title: ESR Essentials: susceptibility-weighted imaging-practice recommendations by the European Society for Magnetic Resonance in Medicine and Biology.
articles.abstract: Susceptibility-weighted imaging (SWI) is a high-resolution 3D gradient-echo (GRE) magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) technique that combines magnitude and phase information to increase sensitivity to blood products, iron, calcification, thrombus, and venous structures. In routine practice, SWI should be interpreted together with source magnitude images, filtered phase images, processed SWI images, and minimum-intensity projection (minIP) images, keeping in mind blooming and other artefacts, as well as vendor-dependent phase conventions. Its most established role is in brain MRI, particularly in: suspected cerebral amyloid angiopathy; baseline and follow-up assessment of amyloid-related imaging abnormalities with haemosiderin deposition (ARIA-H) during anti-amyloid therapy; traumatic brain injury; multiple sclerosis work-up, when assessment of the central vein sign or paramagnetic rim lesions is clinically relevant; neuro-oncology; and vascular malformations. Overall, these constitute the core recommended brain scenarios for SWI supported by moderate to high levels of evidence. Outside neuroradiology (e.g., musculoskeletal, abdominal, breast, pelvic, and cardiac imaging), SWI remains promising but less standardised and should currently be reserved for selected problem-solving indications. KEY POINTS: SWI should be acquired as a high-resolution 3D GRE sequence and interpreted together with source magnitude images, filtered phase images, and post-processed minIP images, keeping in mind blooming and other artefacts, as well as vendor-specific phase conventions. SWI should be included in brain MRI protocols when haemorrhagic or microvascular susceptibility findings are expected to affect diagnosis or management, especially in cerebral amyloid angiopathy, anti-amyloid therapy monitoring, traumatic brain injury, and neuro-oncology or multiple sclerosis work-up. Outside neuroradiology, SWI can be used as a targeted problem-solving adjunct rather than as a routine sequence.

articles.title: A latent ODE approach to full-cycle biventricular cardiac motion modeling from cine MRI.
articles.abstract: Cardiac magnetic resonance imaging (CMR) captures rich spatiotemporal information about ventricular structure and motion, but conventional risk models use only a few image-derived indices from selected cardiac phases. We present a latent dynamical model that encodes bi-ventricular anatomy and full-cycle cine motion as a continuous latent trajectory, using heart-rate-aware neural ordinary differential equation (ODE) dynamics and a graph-based mesh autoencoder to reconstruct anatomically consistent 3D+t ventricular motion. A covariate-conditioned prior defines the expected end-diastolic latent state, and a Cox proportional hazards model tests whether deviations from this prior predict incident heart failure. We studied 72,386 UK Biobank participants without baseline cardiovascular disease, including 367 incident heart failure events. In a held-out evaluation subset, adding the latent score to refitted pooled cohort equations improved the stratified C-index from 0.704 to 0.785, compared with 0.764 for seven established cardiac markers. Compared with non-graph and non-ODE approaches, the proposed model gave the best trade-off between reconstruction fidelity, generative realism, and downstream prognostic performance. These results suggest that continuous full-cycle modeling of ventricular motion provides informative cardiac phenotypes beyond conventional CMR summaries, while external validation in more representative patient cohorts is required before clinical risk-prediction use.

articles.title: Joint segmentation of pancreatic tumors and peripancreatic vessels via a clinical risk-aware uncertainty alignment framework.
articles.abstract: Preoperative assessment of pancreatic cancer resectability critically relies on accurate joint segmentation of tumors and peripancreatic vessels from contrast-enhanced CT. However, beyond segmentation accuracy alone, effective decision support in practice further requires task-specific characterization of peri‑tumoral infiltration risk and topological discontinuity risk. To address this, we propose a clinical risk-aware uncertainty alignment framework that achieves reliable risk characterization while maintaining high segmentation accuracy. The framework is built upon a dual-decoder architecture with evidential deep learning for joint segmentation and uncertainty estimation. Two clinically grounded alignment strategies are further designed to transform this uncertainty into task-specific risk indicators. Specifically, an infiltration-aware boundary uncertainty alignment module is proposed, which synthesizes texture, spatial, and vascular proximity factors into an infiltration-inspired prior and uses its ordinal structure to guide alignment, yielding infiltration-risk-aware uncertainty from which infiltration-aware tumor boundaries are derived for downstream invasion analysis. A topology-aware discontinuity uncertainty alignment module is further designed, which uses skeleton-mismatch regions as a connectivity-related proxy and constrains uncertainty by a three-tier ordinal relation with region-weighted supervision, yielding discontinuity-risk-aware uncertainty and improved vessel connectivity. Multi-center validation on 1058 patients from five medical centers demonstrates favorable and stable cross-institutional performance, and downstream experiments explore the utility of the aligned uncertainty for tumor-vessel invasion analysis. Overall, this study couples accurate tumor and vessel delineation with clinically grounded risk characterization, with the potential to support tumor-vessel assessment in preoperative planning. Our source code will be released at https://github.com/SJTUBME-QianLab/CRUA-Net.

articles.title: AI-based diagnosis of frontotemporal dementia using neuroimaging: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVE: This meta-analysis aimed to evaluate the diagnostic accuracy of neuroimaging-based artificial intelligence (AI) models for detecting frontotemporal dementia (FTD) and its primary clinical subtypes. MATERIALS AND METHODS: A systematic search of PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, and Cochrane Library was conducted up to October 22, 2025. Studies reporting neuroimaging-based AI model performance for diagnosing FTD variants against cognitively normal (CN) controls were included. Study quality and outcome certainty were assessed using the PROBAST + AI tool and GRADE. A bivariate random-effects model was used to calculate pooled sensitivity, specificity, and the area under the curve (AUC). RESULTS: Twenty-three studies involving 3670 subjects were included. AI models demonstrated a pooled sensitivity of 0.91 (95% CI: 0.87-0.93; I2 = 73.2%), specificity of 0.92 (95% CI: 0.89-0.94; I2 = 80.2%), and an AUC of 0.96 (95% CI: 0.94-0.98). Subtype analysis revealed the highest performance for semantic variant primary progressive aphasia (svPPA), with an AUC of 0.98 (95% CI: 0.97-0.99). Across neuroimaging modalities (sMRI, fMRI, PET, and multimodal), AUC values remained consistently robust, ranging from 0.94 to 0.98. Notably, a temporal analysis indicated a slight declining trend in reported AUC values from 2009 to 2025, though most models maintained an AUC above 0.90. CONCLUSIONS: Neuroimaging-based AI models show promising diagnostic performance for FTD, especially for the svPPA subtype, supporting their potential as a clinical adjunct. However, the evidence certainty is limited by frequent high risk of bias and study heterogeneity. Prospective, multicenter validation is required to confirm generalizability and clinical utility. REGISTRATION NUMBER: CRD420251270006. KEY POINTS: Question Can neuroimaging-based artificial intelligence accurately distinguish frontotemporal dementia and its major clinical subtypes from cognitively normal controls in published diagnostic studies? Findings Across 23 studies, pooled accuracy was high, but estimates were limited by heterogeneity, small subgroup samples, and frequent validation bias. Clinical relevance AI models may support FTD diagnostic workflows, but current evidence favors cautious adjunctive use rather than stand-alone clinical implementation until prospective external validation improves.

articles.title: Shear-wave elastography in rotator cuff tears: a systematic review of measurement properties, tissue-stiffness findings, and clinical interpretability.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVES: Shear-wave elastography (SWE) may quantify rotator cuff mechanical properties, but its measurement performance and clinical interpretability remain incompletely established. This work sought to synthesize evidence on the feasibility, measurement properties, and interpretability of rotator cuff SWE in adults with rotator cuff tears (RCTs). MATERIALS AND METHODS: PubMed, Scopus, and Web of Science were searched. Eligible studies were in vivo primary studies in adults (≥ 18 years) with suspected or symptomatic rotator cuff disease in whom partial- or full-thickness RCT was confirmed by an imaging or surgical reference standard, including conventional ultrasound, MRI, CT, or arthroscopy, and/or studies including clinically relevant comparator shoulders or asymptomatic controls. Studies had to use ultrasound SWE with quantitative outputs, including shear-wave speed/velocity or modulus, in the supraspinatus tendon and/or rotator cuff muscles. RESULTS: Thirteen SWE studies were retained from 6273 records. Two primarily assessed reliability/repeatability. Intra-rater reproducibility was high in the primary reliability studies, including ICCs > 0.87 and 0.96, whereas inter-rater reproducibility was lower and variable, ranging from ICCs > 0.73 to 0.45. Eleven studies contributed construct-validity or known-groups evidence, one provided strict criterion-validity evidence against intraoperative passive stiffness, and two provided longitudinal postoperative evidence. SWE findings varied across tissue targets, devices, regions of interest, arm positions, comparators, and reference standards. Only one study explicitly defined chronicity, and direct postoperative/prognostic evidence was limited. CONCLUSIONS: SWE appears useful as a complementary quantitative imaging tool for selected rotator cuff tissue-characterization and measurement-property applications. However, inter-rater reproducibility, measurement error, chronicity assessment, and prognostic validity remain insufficiently established. KEY POINTS: Question Can shear-wave elastography (SWE) address the unmet need for reliable quantitative rotator cuff tissue assessment beyond conventional imaging in adults with tears? Findings Thirteen studies showed high intra-rater reproducibility but variable inter-rater reproducibility. Evidence for chronicity assessment and prognosis remained sparse and heterogeneous. Clinical relevance SWE may complement ultrasound or MRI by quantifying selected rotator cuff mechanical properties, but current evidence does not justify using it alone to determine tear chronicity, reparability, or prognosis.

articles.title: Stent Configurations in Aortoiliac Occlusive disease: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: To evaluate which endovascular stent configuration at the aortic bifurcation offers superior outcomes for aorto-iliac occlusive disease (AIOD). METHODS: Studies reporting outcomes for endovascular reconstruction for AIOD, for TransAtlantic Inter-Society Consensus (TASC) C and D lesions were included in the review. Data for primary, primary-assisted and secondary patency were extracted (full-text articles or reconstructed from published Kaplan Meier curves). RESULTS: This review included 12 studies, including 1027 patients (177 Covered Endovascular Reconstruction of the Aortic Bifurcation (CERAB), 850 kissing stent). Most studies were retrospective cohort studies with moderate methodological quality. Median follow-up was 20 months for primary patency, and 48 months for assisted and secondary patency. CERAB and kissing stent techniques showed similar primary patency (p=0.24). Primary-assisted patency was slightly lower for CERAB but not statistically significant (p=0.051). Secondary patency favored CERAB (p=0.045). At two years, CERAB had primary patency of 90%, primary-assisted patency of 87%, and secondary patency of 100%. Kissing stents showed primary patency of 91%, primary-assisted patency of 92%, and secondary patency of 96%. CONCLUSION: Both stent types yielded positive results, but current data does not favor one configuration. Current studies on this topic are low quality. At present, the method of endovascular intervention for AIOD could be left to clinical expertise, although hemodynamic studies may provide insights. Randomized trial data or post-market registries are needed to ascertain superiority of any stent configuration in this disease process.

articles.title: Comparative Effectiveness and Safety of Treatments and Embolic Agents for Symptomatic Uterine Fibroids: A Bayesian Network Meta-analysis.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: To compare, using Bayesian network meta-analysis, the effectiveness and safety of treatments and embolic agents for symptomatic uterine fibroids. MATERIALS AND METHODS: A PRISMA-compliant systematic review of randomized controlled trials (PubMed, Embase, Cochrane Library; inception through July 2026) compared, via two prespecified Bayesian network meta-analyses, (1) uterine artery embolization (UAE) with hysterectomy, myomectomy, magnetic resonance-guided focused ultrasound, microwave ablation, and laparoscopic uterine artery occlusion, and (2) embolic agents used during UAE. Primary outcomes were technical success and major complications for treatment strategies, and complete/near-complete fibroid infarction for embolic agents; reintervention was secondary in both networks. RESULTS: Twenty-three RCTs (N=2,055 women) were included. Technical success and major complication rates did not differ significantly across treatment strategies or embolic agents in the Bayesian analysis, though frequentist analysis showed slightly higher technical success with hysterectomy than UAE (RR, 1.09; 95% CI, 1.02-1.17). Myomectomy had significantly lower reintervention than UAE (OR, 0.21; 95% CrI, 0.10-0.40). Several Bayesian associations emerged for polyvinyl alcohol (PVA) particles versus tris-acryl gelatin microspheres (TAGM), including higher complete infarction (OR, 4.8; 95% CrI, 1.0-40), higher reintervention (OR, 5.3; 95% CrI, 1.4-28), and divergent findings with PVA700-900; none was reproduced in the frequentist analysis. CONCLUSION: UAE did not differ significantly from alternative strategies in procedural success or safety, but myomectomy showed greater durability. Evidence is insufficient to establish definitive embolic-agent differences. Treatment strategy appears to influence outcomes more than embolic material, supporting individualized selection and larger trials.

articles.title: Transfemoral transcaval adrenal biopsy: a technical report and review of adrenal biopsy approaches.
articles.abstract: Despite advances in cross-sectional imaging, adrenal biopsy plays a role in a small subset of lesions that remain indeterminate after complete imaging work-up or in which tissue diagnosis would alter management. Anatomic constraints around the adrenal glands can make safe percutaneous access technically challenging. This technical report describes a transfemoral transcaval approach to biopsy of a right adrenal mass directly abutting the inferior vena cava (IVC) that was not safely accessible by conventional percutaneous routes. Additionally, a concise review of contemporary adrenal biopsy indications and access routes is performed. Adapted from transfemoral transcaval liver biopsy, the technique uses right common femoral venous access, positioning of a reshaped metal guide cannula within the IVC at the level of the lesion adjacent to the right renal vein, and deployment of a core biopsy needle across the caval wall under combined fluoroscopic and ultrasound guidance, with cone-beam CT confirmation of needle position and completion venography to exclude caval injury. Diagnostic tissue was obtained without periprocedural complication; histopathology demonstrated an unexpected pheochromocytoma, a finding discussed here in detail due to its implications for pre-procedure biochemical evaluation. This limited experience demonstrates technical feasibility in carefully selected patients. The safety and comparative effectiveness of the technique require evaluation in larger series.

articles.title: A new bone lesion or an aging marrow phenotype? Rethinking bilateral distal femoral sclerosis.
COLLATERAL EMBOLIZATION IN THE ENDOVASCULAR TREATMENT OF PORTAL CAVERNOMA CHOLANGIOPATHY: A POTENTIAL CAUSE OF SEVERE BILIARY OBSTRUCTION.
articles.abstract: Management of complicated portal cavernoma cholangiopathy (PCC) remains nonstandardized. When biliary drainage fails, portal vein recanalization with transjugular intrahepatic portosystemic shunt (PVR-TIPS) is increasingly considered and may require collateral embolization during the procedure. This work describes two patients with complicated PCC in whom collateral embolization during or after PVR-TIPS caused severe biliary obstruction requiring long-term biliary drainage. A narrative review was conducted, identifying 18 published studies describing patients with PCC who underwent endovascular treatment. Collateral embolization was inconsistently reported, and its biliary consequences were rarely described. Severe biliary obstruction following peribiliary collateral embolization may therefore be an underrecognized complication; however, its incidence remains unknown based on the available literature. Thus, when collateral embolization is considered during endovascular treatment of PCC, its potential biliary risk should be weighed, and the anatomical relationship between the targeted collaterals and the bile duct carefully assessed.

articles.title: Non-contrast MR Neurography for the evaluation of Facial Nerve Neuropathy in patients with Facial Synkinesis - a comparative case-control study.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND AND PURPOSE: Facial synkinesis is a debilitating sequela of peripheral facial nerve palsy, yet objective imaging characterization of the affected facial nerve remains limited. We evaluated the discrimination performance of non-contrast peripheral MR neurography (MRN) using 3D PSIF in patients with facial synkinesis. MATERIALS AND METHODS: In this retrospective case-control study, non-contrast MRN images of 32 adults with unilateral facial synkinesis (28 Bell's palsy, 4 Ramsay Hunt syndrome) and 30 controls (29 occipital neuralgia, 1 TMJ pain) were independently reviewed by two fellowship-trained radiologists. Discrimination performance of 3D PSIF was calculated from 2 × 2 tables against cases versus controls, compared with bFFE using McNemar's test, and inter-reader reliability quantified using Cohen's κ. RESULTS: 3D PSIF demonstrated high accuracy for facial neuropathy detection (Reader 1: 93.5%, sensitivity 90.6%, specificity 96.7%; Reader 2: 91.9%, sensitivity 87.5%, specificity 96.7%). Compared to bFFE in the paired subset (n = 59), 3D PSIF demonstrated substantially higher sensitivity than bFFE (sensitivity 86.7% vs 30.0%; equivalent specificity 96.6%; McNemar p < 0.001). The mastoid and extratemporal segments were the most involved, while the canalicular and labyrinthine segments were not involved in any case. Inter-reader agreement was almost perfect for signal abnormality (κ = 0.97), increased nerve thickness (κ = 0.97), and segmental patterns (full agreement in 53/62 patients, 85.5%). CONCLUSIONS: In this single-center, proof-of-concept study, non-contrast 3D PSIF reliably identified facial nerve abnormality in facial synkinesis and outperformed bFFE, with predominantly distal nerve involvement. A prospective multi-center validation is needed before these findings can inform clinical practice.

articles.title: After-hours on-site radiologist availability and emergency CT reporting: a roster-based cohort with staffing-boundary analysis.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: To compare after-hours emergency CT report turnaround during periods with versus without roster-recorded on-site CT radiologist availability. MATERIALS AND METHODS: This retrospective roster-based cohort included emergency-department CT examinations from 1 July 2025 to 30 June 2026. The common-support cohort comprised non-holiday weekdays from 15:00 to 06:59 and all weekends and public holidays. Components within 15 min were grouped into packages. The exposure was on-site CT radiologist availability recorded in the final as-worked duty roster; actual reporting route was secondary. The primary outcome was scan-to-complete-report turnaround time (TAT). Models used duty-date-clustered standard errors and adjusted for patient, temporal, workload, and examination characteristics. RESULTS: The cohort contained 13,533 CT packages; 13,270 had usable TAT and 12,333 index encounters were clinically linked. Median TAT was 81 min without and 58 min with an on-site radiologist. Absence of an on-site radiologist was associated with 33.9% longer adjusted TAT (95% CI 25.4-43.0). The association was 28.4% for routine non-contrast head CT and 45.5% for abdominopelvic CT (interaction + 15.1%; p = 0.001). A ± 120-minute staffing-boundary analysis estimated 45.7% longer TAT (16.3-82.5), with positive estimates across ± 60- to ± 180-minute bandwidths and no detected covariate discontinuities. Actual-route TAT was 47.7% longer amid 34.5% route discordance. CONCLUSION: During comparable after-hours periods, roster-recorded absence of an on-site CT radiologist was associated with longer complete-report TAT, particularly for abdominopelvic CT. Downstream stay differences were exploratory and may reflect broader hospital processes.

articles.title: Predicting Signal Intensity Profiles for Various MRI Contrast Agent Injection Strategies: Including Measurement of Relaxivities in Oxygenated Whole Human Blood for Gadopiclenol, Gadoterate Meglumine and Gadoteridol.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Gadolinium based contrast agents (GBCAs) vary in arterial signal intensity (SI) profiles. Gadopiclenol is a high relaxivity GBCA approved at 0.05 mmol/kg. PURPOSE: Evaluate contrast-enhanced MRA injection strategies: measure r1, r2, and r2* of gadopiclenol, gadoterate meglumine, and gadoteridol in plasma and blood, and model arterial SI profiles for different injection rates. STUDY TYPE: Phantom/Modeling. PHANTOM: Vials of oxygenated whole blood and plasma, with gadopiclenol, gadoterate meglumine, and gadoteridol ranging from 1 to 18 mM. FIELDSTRENGTH/SEQUENCE: Look-Locker, multi-echo turbo spin echo (mTSE), multi-echo fast field echo (mFFE) at 1.5 T and 3.0 T. ASSESSMENT: R1 derived by mono-exponential recovery fitting of Look-Locker data. R2 and R2* derived by fitting mono-exponential decays of mTSE and mFFE data. r1plasma, r2plasma,blood, r2plasma,blood* derived by linear fitting of R1, R2, R2* versus GBCA concentration [GBCA]. R1blood predicted using fast-exchange-regime (FXR) and -limit (FXL), compared with measured R1blood. Spoiled gradient echo (SPGR) SI versus [GBCA] modeled at 1.5 T and 3.0 T for each GBCA and two SPGR protocols using these blood relaxivities, generating SI versus time curves at rates of 0.5, 1, and 2 mL/s. STATISTICAL TESTS: Trust reflective least squares algorithm, Levenberg-Marquardt least squares curve fitting, FXR and FXL prediction models. RESULTS: Gadopiclenol r1plasma, r2plasma, r2plasma* ~3 times greater than gadoteridol and gadoterate meglumine. R1blood, well-predicted by FXR (RMSE 4.6 vs. 28 s-1 for FXL). Gadopiclenol r2blood* 20%-46% higher than the other contrast agents, with r2 blood similar across agents (7.4-8.8 s-1 mM-1 at 1.5 T and 12.9-13.4 s-1 mM-1 at 3.0 T). CE-MRA modeling demonstrated slight SI decrease at 1 versus 2 mL/s (0%-14% SI loss generally; 2%-6% for gadopiclenol), with a more uniform arterial enhancement profile. CONCLUSION: SI profiles vary for different GBCAs. Modeling showed injection rates as low as 1.0 mL/s (or 0.5 mL/s for gadopiclenol and gadobutrol) may provide benefit. TECHNICAL EFFICACY: Stage 3.

articles.title: Temporal ROI-Based Framework for Automated Multi-Criterion Critical View of Safety Assessment in Laparoscopic Cholecystectomy.
articles.abstract: Accurate assessment of the Critical View of Safety (CVS) during laparoscopic cholecystectomy is essential to prevent bile duct injuries. Automated CVS assessment from surgical videos remains challenging due to complex anatomy, instrument occlusion, and the temporal nature of dissection. However, existing methods rely on full-frame processing without focusing on anatomically relevant regions, limiting both efficiency and anatomical specificity. We propose a region-of-interest (ROI)-based spatio-temporal framework for automated multi-criterion CVS classification that explicitly models anatomical relationships and surgical progression using the multi-modal Endoscapes dataset. Rather than processing full frames, our pipeline extracts anatomically relevant ROIs guided by bounding box annotations, models intra-frame structural dependencies via a Graph Attention Network and captures surgical progression through a bi-directional LSTM with temporal attention. Complementary segmentation masks are leveraged to validate that model attention aligns with true anatomical boundaries. Evaluated on the Endoscapes test set, our method achieves 70.8% mean Average Precision (mAP), 74.6% balanced accuracy for multi-criterion classification, and an Area Under the ROC Curve (AUC) of 86.8% for overall CVS assessment, outperforming representative full-frame baselines. The model demonstrates high specificity (> 90%) and clinically interpretable attention maps that consistently localize to Calot's triangle and cystic structures. By decoupling spatial detection from temporal reasoning and exploiting multi-modal annotations, this work advances automated surgical safety assessment through clinically grounded ROI processing and expressive spatio-temporal modelling.

articles.title: Anatomical VOI-based assessment of the three DESH components in probable idiopathic normal pressure hydrocephalus.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: To evaluate whether anatomical volume-of-interest (VOI) thresholds derived from a SINPHONI-2 reference cohort could provide standardized component-wise quantification of disproportionately enlarged subarachnoid-space hydrocephalus (DESH) in a separate clinical cohort. MATERIALS AND METHODS: Thresholds were derived from 61 SINPHONI-2 cases using a prespecified mildest-case rule and applied without re-optimization to 33 participants with probable idiopathic normal pressure hydrocephalus (iNPH), 26 with Alzheimer disease, 18 with progressive supranuclear palsy, and 20 normal controls. DESH metric-S summed binary positivity for ventriculomegaly, Sylvian fissure enlargement, and tight high-convexity and medial sulci; DESH metric-I was defined as (Sylvian fissure volume + lateral ventricular volume)/high-convexity and medial sulcal volume. Evans index and callosal angle were evaluated as conventional imaging measures. RESULTS: For iNPH versus pooled non-iNPH, DESH metric-S had an area under the curve (AUC) of 0.958 (95% CI, 0.921-0.990), sensitivity of 97.0% (84.7-99.5%), and specificity of 92.2% (83.0-96.6%). DESH metric-I had an AUC of 0.995 (95% CI, 0.983-1.000), sensitivity of 100.0% (89.6-100.0%), and specificity of 93.8% (85.0-97.5%). CONCLUSION: Anatomical VOI-based measures provided standardized component-wise quantification of DESH morphology. DESH metric-S retained the status of each component, whereas DESH metric-I provided a continuous summary. Because DESH contributed to probable-iNPH classification, the observed discrimination reflects concordance with a DESH-supported classification rather than independent diagnostic accuracy for iNPH. External validation, including cohorts spanning incomplete/non-DESH morphology and treatment-response outcomes, is required before clinical or prognostic use.

articles.title: Ultrafast brain MRI at 3 T for suspected acute ischemic stroke: interchangeability of the ultrafast and standard protocols.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: To evaluate the interchangeability of the super-resolution deep learning reconstruction (SR-DLR)-based ultrafast protocol with the standard protocol for acute ischemic stroke detection at 3 T. MATERIALS AND METHODS: In this prospective study, 100 patients (mean age, 66.1 ± 16.2 years; 65 men) with suspected acute ischemic stroke underwent both the standard and ultrafast protocols (diffusion-weighted, fluid-attenuated inversion recovery, and T2*-weighted imaging). All images were reconstructed using SR-DLR; the ultrafast protocol employed accelerated acquisition with a reduced scan time. Two radiologists independently assessed both protocols for acute ischemic lesion detection, vascular territory involvement, and clinically relevant secondary findings. Interchangeability was evaluated using the individual equivalence index (IEI), with a prespecified ± 0.05 equivalence margin. RESULTS: Acute ischemic stroke was confirmed in 30 patients (30%). The ultrafast protocol reduced the mean total acquisition time by 61.7% (1 min 43 s vs. 4 min 29 s; P < 0.001). Interchangeability was demonstrated for patient-level acute ischemic lesion detection (IEI, 0.010 [90% confidence interval (CI): -0.006, 0.026]), vascular territory-level detection (IEIs, - 0.007 to 0.015), and clinically relevant secondary findings (IEI, 0.005 [90% CI: -0.025, 0.035]). Qualitative image quality scores were slightly but consistently higher for the ultrafast protocol across all four assessment items (all P ≤ 0.002). No significant differences were observed in ischemic lesion size or relative signal characteristics between protocols. CONCLUSION: The ultrafast protocol was interchangeable with the standard protocol for detecting acute ischemic stroke, with reduced scan time and comparable or marginally improved image quality; however, this work-in-progress diffusion-weighted imaging algorithm warrants further validation.

articles.title: Beyond the heart: a large-cohort study of 11C-PiB PET revealing organ-specific uptake patterns and diagnostic thresholds in systemic AL amyloidosis.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: Systemic AL amyloidosis frequently involves multiple organs, yet non‑invasive imaging for early and comprehensive multi‑organ assessment remains limited. The diagnostic role of 11C-PiB PET beyond the heart-particularly its organ‑specific uptake patterns and clinically applicable thresholds-has not been systematically defined in a large cohort. MATERIALS AND METHODS: This retrospective study included 80 participants (60 ± 10 years, 55 males) undergoing Whole-body 11C-PiB PET/MR or PET/CT from 2018 to Sep 2024. Final diagnoses were as follows: AL group (n = 65), non‑AL group (n = 10), control group (n = 5). PET indices (SUVmax, SUVRmax, ASUVRmax, ASUVRmean) were quantified for 15 organs. Optimal diagnostic cutoffs were derived using ROC analysis or quartiles. Correlations with clinical and morphofunctional markers were assessed. RESULTS: Organ-specific uptake patterns differed across tissues, with clear disease-related accumulation observed in the myocardium, spleen, bone marrow, and tongue, whereas interpretation was limited in organs affected by physiological tracer kinetics, such as the kidney. Myocardial PiB uptake correlated significantly with NT‑proBNP, native T1, and ventricular wall thickness; hepatic uptake was paradoxically reduced, with negative correlations with ALP and projected liver area; renal uptake correlated positively with eGFR and negatively with β2‑microglobulin. Organ-specific diagnostic thresholds were established using the optimal-performing semiquantitative parameters: myocardium SUVmax 2.20 (sensitivity 90%, specificity 100%, AUC 0.995); tongue SUVmax 2.05 (86%, 100%, AUC 0.971); bone marrow SUVRmax 2.05 (70%, 100%, AUC 0.880); liver SUVmax 7.95 (88%, 80%, AUC 0.900). Quartile‑based thresholds further defined involvement in the spleen, thyroid, and salivary glands. CONCLUSIONS: In this study, 11C-PiB PET revealed distinct organ-specific uptake patterns and diagnostic thresholds for systemic AL amyloidosis across multiple organs were preliminarily established. It provides a non-invasive, biopsy‑sparing assessment of multi-organ involvement while highlighting organ-specific limitations, particularly related to renal uptake interpretation and the need for further validation in selected tissues.

articles.title: MRI-based deep learning model for prediction of Ki-67 expression level in intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Ki-67 expression is a valuable prognostic indicator in intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma (iCCA). This study aimed to develop a non-invasive Deep learning (DL) model based on magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) and clinical data to predict Ki-67 expression preoperatively. METHODS: Patients with iCCA between January 2020 and January 2024 were retrospectively reviewed. Based on immunohistochemistry, patients were classified into high-expression group (Ki-67 > 50%) and low-expression group (Ki-67 ≤ 50%). After image acquisition, tumor segmentation, and preprocessing, a 3D-ResNet10 network was utilized for MRI feature extraction. A feed-forward neural network (FFN) was used for clinical feature extraction. Subsequently, the extracted image and clinical features were fused and fed into a lightweight classifier to perform Ki-67 level prediction. The performance of the DL models was evaluated via 5-fold cross-validation using accuracy, precision, sensitivity, specificity, F1-score, and the area under the curve (AUC). RESULTS: A total of 117 patients were ultimately included (30 cases in the high-expression group and 87 cases in the low-expression group). The model based solely on clinical variables demonstrated limited predictive efficacy (mean AUC: 53.18 ± 14.60%). The model utilizing MRI features alone exhibited high specificity (86.14 ± 10.25%) but modest sensitivity. In contrast, the fused DL model significantly outperformed both individual models, attaining a mean AUC of 84.24 ± 8.82%, an accuracy of 87.17 ± 5.95%, a specificity of 93.07 ± 9.35%, and a markedly improved sensitivity of 70.00 ± 19.44%, yielding a robust F1-score of 73.42 ± 12.28%. CONCLUSIONS: We developed and validated a non-invasive DL model integrating contrast-enhanced MRI and clinical parameters that accurately predicts Ki-67 expression in iCCA, demonstrating superior diagnostic performance.

articles.title: Pretreatment prediction of neoadjuvant therapy response in locally advanced gastric cancer using an additive ctSLEP score and spectral CT.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: To develop an additive ctSLEP score from routine CT morphologic invasion signs and evaluate the complementary value of morphologic CT, quantitative spectral CT, and systemic inflammation for pretreatment prediction of neoadjuvant therapy (NAT) response in locally advanced gastric cancer (LAGC). METHODS: This retrospective study included 158 patients with LAGC who underwent NAT and radical gastrectomy and were randomly divided into training and internal validation cohorts (7:3). Becker tumor regression grade 1a/1b defined response and 2/3 nonresponse. Additive ctSLEP summed four pretreatment CT signs: serosal invasion, extramural venous invasion, subtle signs of occult peritoneal/omental involvement, and lymphovascular invasion. Five hierarchical models combined additive ctSLEP, venous-phase iodine concentration (ICVP), arterial enhancement fraction (AEF), and neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (NLR). Performance was assessed using AUC, Brier score, calibration, and prespecified paired DeLong comparisons. A chemotherapy-only sensitivity analysis was performed. RESULTS: Sixty-five patients (41.1%) were responders and ninety-three (58.9%) nonresponders. In the internal validation cohort, AUCs for the Morphology, Spectral, Imaging, Clinical-spectral, and Combined models were 0.642, 0.741, 0.725, 0.713, and 0.754, respectively. The Combined model had the highest AUC and lowest Brier score (0.200). Adding spectral CT to morphology increased AUC by 0.083 (P=0.129), and adding additive ctSLEP to the Clinical-spectral model increased AUC by 0.041 (P=0.558). In 51 patients receiving chemotherapy alone, higher additive ctSLEP was associated with greater odds of nonresponse (OR=2.15, 95% CI 1.35-3.88), whereas higher ICVP was associated with lower odds (OR=0.83, 95% CI 0.69-0.96). CONCLUSION: The combined model showed reasonable predictive performance in internal validation. These findings support further external evaluation of a low-dimensional, clinically interpretable strategy integrating morphologic invasion burden, spectral enhancement, and systemic inflammation for pretreatment NAT response stratification.

articles.title: 5.0 T Coronary Magnetic Resonance Angiography in Calcified Coronary Arteries: Diagnostic Performance Compared With Computed Tomography Using Invasive Angiography as Reference.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Coronary computed tomography angiography (CCTA) often overestimates stenosis in calcified plaques due to blooming artifacts. The performance of 5.0 T Coronary MR angiography (CMRA) in calcified arteries remains unclear. PURPOSE: To assess plaque effects on 5.0 T CMRA image quality and compare diagnostic performance with CCTA. STUDY TYPE: Prospective. POPULATION: Forty-six patients with suspected coronary artery disease. FIELD STRENGTH/SEQUENCE: 5.0 T; free-breathing, non-contrast 3D gradient-echo sequence, Dixon water-fat separation, artificial intelligence-assisted compressed sensing. ASSESSMENT: Three blinded radiologists with 6, 8, and 12 years' experience independently evaluated all datasets. Obstructive stenosis was defined as ≥ 50%; CMRA and CCTA image quality used a 4-point scale; quantitative CMRA measures included vessel edge sharpness (VES), signal-to-noise ratio (SNR), and contrast-to-noise ratio (CNR). CCTA assessed plaque composition, calcium burden, and calcification length. Invasive angiography was the reference. STATISTICAL TESTS: Diagnostic metrics and generalized estimating equations evaluated performance and plaque-image-quality associations. Wilcoxon tests compared visual scores. Agreements used Cohen's κ, Fleiss' κ, and intraclass correlation coefficients. RESULTS: 5.0 T CMRA showed higher specificity (90.1% vs. 77.7%, p < 0.001) and accuracy (89.4% vs. 82.8%, p = 0.006) than CCTA, with similar sensitivity (88.7% vs. 87.7%, p = 0.740). For CMRA, VES was lower in segments containing mixed plaques than in noncalcified or calcified plaques (16.0 ± 0.8 vs. 18.2 ± 0.8 and 18.3 ± 1.0; p < 0.001). Visual scores differed across calcium-burden categories (3.35 ± 0.07, 3.16 ± 0.09, 2.96 ± 0.09, and 2.79 ± 0.09; p < 0.001). Greater calcification length was associated with lower VES (B = -0.152, p = 0.008) and visual scores (B = -0.019, p = 0.019). DATA CONCLUSION: In this cohort, 5.0 T CMRA showed higher specificity and accuracy than CCTA, with similar sensitivity. Plaque characteristics were associated with selected CMRA image-quality measures. EVIDENCE LEVEL: 2. TECHNICAL EFFICACY: Stage 2.

articles.title: Multiparametric Quantitative MRI With 2.5D Deep Learning for Molecular Classification and Overall Survival Assessment in Adult-Type Diffuse Gliomas.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Quantitative MRI may enable noninvasive glioma characterization, but optimal analytic strategies and prognostic utility remain uncertain. PURPOSE: To compare volume-of-interest (VOI)-mean, radiomics, and 2D, 2.5D, and 3D deep learning (DL) for preoperative molecular classification and assess the prognostic value of a 2.5D-DL-derived isocitrate dehydrogenase wild-type score (2.5D-IDHwt score) in a postoperative clinicopathologic survival model. STUDY TYPE: Retrospective multicenter study. POPULATION: One thousand four hundred and eight adults with diffuse glioma: training (n = 409), temporal validation (n = 300), and three external test cohorts (n = 119, 310, and 270). FIELD STRENGTH/SEQUENCE: 3 T; spin-echo echo-planar diffusion-weighted imaging, 3D pseudo-continuous arterial spin labeling, and multidynamic multiecho synthetic MRI. ASSESSMENT: Apparent diffusion coefficient, cerebral blood flow, T1, T2, proton-density, and contrast-enhanced T1 maps were generated. Two neuroradiologists (5 and 20 years' experience) delineated whole-tumor VOIs. Six map-specific models were stacked separately for VOI-mean, radiomics, 2D-DL, 2.5D-DL, and 3D-DL. 2.5D-qMR-Clin combined the 2.5D-IDHwt score with age, O6-methylguanine-DNA methyltransferase promoter methylation, and extent of resection and was compared with PathoClin incorporating pathological IDH status. STATISTICAL TESTS: Area under the curve (AUC), DeLong tests, Harrell C-index, bootstrap resampling, calibration, decision-curve analysis, Kaplan-Meier analysis, and Cox regression. p < 0.05 indicated significance. RESULTS: The 2.5D-DL stacking model achieved the highest external AUCs for IDH mutation (0.89-0.93) and 1p/19q codeletion (0.92-0.95), significantly outperforming the other four stacking models. Reverse Kaplan-Meier median follow-up was 1344 days (95% CI, 1316-1383); 27.5% died. External C-indices for 2.5D-qMR-Clin were 0.750, 0.778, and 0.762 versus 0.704, 0.722, and 0.723 for PathoClin, with significant differences in test cohorts 2 and 3. Fixed-cutoff risk stratification was significant across all external cohorts (hazard ratios, 5.30-5.80). A web-based 2.5D-qMR-Clin explorer provided 1-, 2-, and 3-year OS estimates. DATA CONCLUSION: Among evaluated approaches, 2.5D-DL stacking performed best for molecular classification, and the 2.5D-IDHwt score improved OS assessment in the postoperative clinicopathologic model. EVIDENCE LEVEL: 3. TECHNICAL EFFICACY: Stage 2.

articles.title: New heuristic method for cancer classification using gene expression data.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: The aim of this research is to develop and evaluate a novel feature selection method based on a local search algorithm (LSFS) in combination with a genetic algorithm (GA) for cancer classification using high-dimensional gene expression data. METHODS: The study spanned a period between 2022 and 2024, using data from two medical research centers (Sofia, Bulgaria, and Moscow, Russia). More than 30,000 patient records were analyzed using six open datasets as source data. These datasets included information on blood, breast, colon, and other types of cancer from the GEO and TCGA databases. To prepare the data for analysis, the study employed techniques such as normalization, outlier elimination, and logarithmic transformation. Modern machine learning algorithms, such as random forests, support vector machines, and neural networks, were utilized to assess the effectiveness of the proposed method. RESULTS: The LSFS + GA method demonstrated the ability to maximize accuracy, sensitivity, and specificity, as well as other classification metrics. Specifically, classification accuracy improved by 8-15% depending on the dataset, sensitivity by 10-20%, and specificity by 5-10%. Additionally, there was a 12-18% reduction in noise in the data. The effectiveness of the model was demonstrated by a reduction in entropy, indicating an increase in classification confidence of 6-9%. Statistical analysis, including cross-validation and ANOVA, confirmed the statistical significance of the improvements achieved with the new method (p < 0.05). CONCLUSIONS: The developed algorithm enables a substantial reduction in computational complexity while maintaining, or even improving, classification accuracy. This is important for analyzing cancer data, as it helps to ensure more reliable results. The study's findings demonstrate the potential of combining local search methods with genetic algorithms to address high-dimensional classification problems in bioinformatics.

articles.title: A compliant granular jamming gripper for improved robot-assisted surgical instrument handling.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: Granular jamming grippers (GJGs) offer high geometric adaptability and intrinsic safety for robot-assisted surgical instrument handling but struggle with thin, planar instruments. This study investigates whether external pinching through a passive and partly compliant force-leveraging linkage can enhance grasping performance while maintaining a compact and simple design. METHODS: The SCIP-GRIP, a novel GJG with an integrated Scott-Russell linkage to convert vertical down force into horizontal pinching, was developed. The performances of three gripper versions with varying pinching heights were compared to that of a non-pinching GJG across three instrument types: scalpel (flat), forceps (vertical surfaces), and scissors (undercuts). Both, holding forces and pickup success rates were evaluated using a Universal Testing Machine. Holding forces were measured 12 times per case, while success rates were assessed over 50 trials each. RESULTS: Pinching improves performance across all instruments, with the largest gains observed for scissors, achieving holding forces above 10 N. For forceps and scalpels, only the lowest pinching height yields significant improvements. Success rates for scissors and forceps remain at 100 %, while scalpel success improves from 4 % to 18 % only at low pinching height. Higher pinching heights fail consistently. Performance strongly depends on pinching height, with increased height reducing effectiveness. CONCLUSION: The SCIP-GRIP demonstrates that a passive Scott-Russell linkage can enhance GJG performance while preserving simplicity and safety but pinching below 3 mm is necessary. The design achieves comparable performance to active systems at lower complexity, though further improvements are needed to reliably grasp flat geometries.

articles.title: Temporal MRI appearance of postoperative healing after proximal hamstring musculotendinous complex repair.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVE: To describe the temporal MRI features of healing during the first 4 months following surgical repair of complete tears of the proximal hamstring musculotendinous complex. MATERIALS AND METHODS: Consecutive case series. Professional football players with MRI-confirmed complete tears surgically repaired between May 2017 and December 2025 were retrospectively identified. Postoperative MRI examinations were obtained during routine clinical follow-up using 3-T systems. Two musculoskeletal radiologists independently evaluated longitudinal and transverse intratendinous clefts, scar maturation, edema-like signal, postoperative subcutaneous soft-tissue signal change, tendinous angulation, blunt muscle outline, and denervation-like signal. RESULTS: Twenty-four complete tears in 20 players underwent surgical repair. Fifteen tendons with an uncomplicated postoperative course comprised the primary descriptive cohort, yielding 43 MRI examinations. Longitudinal intratendinous clefts were observed in 11/15 (73.3%) of tendons, transverse intratendinous clefts in 13/15 (86.7%), postoperative subcutaneous soft-tissue signal change and tendinous angulation in 15/15 (100%), blunt muscle outline in 13/15 (86.7%), and denervation-like signal in 10/15 (66.7%). In the within-tendon analysis, longitudinal and transverse intratendinous clefts resolved by the last available MRI in 6/10 (60%) and 7/12 (58.3%) tendons, respectively. All 10 tendons with an initially immature scar progressed to a mature scar. Among six tendons with postoperative exacerbation, four showed extensive, prominent intratendinous clefts with marked PD-FS hyperintensity on the preceding MRI, associated with immature scar, intratendinous cavity, or persistent interstitial edema-like signal. CONCLUSION: Serial MRI demonstrated different temporal patterns of postoperative healing. Residual intratendinous clefts may coexist with a mature scar during tendon remodeling and do not necessarily indicate delayed healing.

articles.title: Work Stress, Burnout and Depression among Radiology Residents: The Moderating Effect of Environment.
articles.abstract: RATIONALE AND OBJECTIVES: This study aimed to explore the modulating role of work environment in the association of work stress with burnout and depression during standardized residency training (SRT) in China. STUDY DESIGN: Nationwide cross-sectional survey. METHOD: A nationwide cross-sectional online survey was conducted among radiology residents in China from December 2020 to April 2021. Participants self-assessed work stress, burnout, depressive symptoms, and work environment satisfaction. Multiple linear regression was used to examine whether the work environment modulated the associations between work stress and burnout and depression. RESULTS: Among 3666 radiology residents surveyed, the average age was 28 years, with 58% identifying as female. Approximately 25.8% reported experiencing burnout, while 24.4% indicated symptoms of depression. Work environment significantly modulated the association between work stress and burnout symptoms (β = -0.23, p = 0.004), but did not significantly moderate the association between work stress and depressive symptoms (β = -0.03, p = 0.423). CONCLUSION: This study found that the work environment significantly moderated the positive association between work stress and burnout among radiology residents, but not the association between work stress and depressive symptoms. A work environment characterized by a stronger sense of safety and a better workplace atmosphere may improve residents' satisfaction with the work environment, thereby enhancing work efficiency and well-being.

articles.title: 3D CEST imaging for differentiating malignant and benign prostatic areas: Diagnostic performance relative to DWI.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: In contrast to diffusion-weighted imaging (DWI) and dynamic contrast-enhanced perfusion MRI, different information from chemical exchange saturation transfer (CEST) imaging has been suggested to have potential for diagnosis of prostate cancer. The purpose of this study was to compare the descriptor capability for differentiating malignant from benign prostatic areas among three-dimensional (3D) amide proton transfer weighted (APTw) imaging using a newly developed 3D CEST sequence, DWI, and the combined descriptor method. MATERIALS AND METHODS: Fifty-two prostate cancer patients underwent DWI and 3D APTw imaging, surgical treatments, and pathological examinations. Then, 154 areas were identified as malignant, and 154 out of 624 areas were computationally selected as benign. From 3D APTw imaging and DWI, magnetization transfer ratio asymmetry (MTRasym) in the 3.5 ppm map and apparent diffusion coefficient (ADC) within malignant and benign prostatic areas were determined by ROI measurements. Then, a logistic regression analysis was conducted to evaluate the descriptors. An ROC analysis and McNemar's test were conducted to compare the diagnostic performance of MTRasym, ADC, and the combined discriminator method. RESULTS: The logistic regression analysis identified MTRasym (unit odds ratio: 3.6, p < 0.0001) and ADC (unit odds ratio: 0.03, p < 0.0001) as significant descriptors. The area under the curve (AUC) of the combined descriptor method (AUC = 0.86) was significantly larger than that of MTRasym (AUC = 0.81, p = 0.001) and ADC (AUC = 0.76, p < 0.0001). CONCLUSION: 3D APTw imaging is considered at least as valuable as DWI to distinguish malignant from benign prostatic areas. Combined descriptors could improve diagnostic performance, relative to each sequence alone.

articles.title: A comparative study of effectiveness and safety of percutaneous cryoablation and microwave ablation of renal cell carcinoma.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: To evaluate differences in technical aspects, safety, and efficacy between percutaneous cryoablation (CRA) and microwave ablation (MWA) for cT1a renal cell carcinoma (RCC). METHODS: From 2013 to 2021, patients with cT1a RCC treated with CRA or MWA were retrospectively included. Baseline characteristics, peri- and post-procedural variables, complications, adverse events, and overall-survival were evaluated. RESULTS: 277 patients were included (214 CRA; 63 MWA). Compared to MWA, CRA was associated with more probes (2.0 (1.0-3.0) vs 1.0 (1.0-2.0) probes; p < 0.0001) and longer procedural time (90 vs 67 min; p = 0.001). CRA was associated with utilization in tumors closer to collecting system (4.0 mm vs 6.0 mm; p = 0.04), a higher any-size hematoma incidence (28% vs 13%; p = 0.01), and incidence of inadvertent critical structure involvement (9% vs 2%; p = 0.02). There was no difference in laboratory adverse events at 12-months (54% vs 44%, p = 0.1), Clavien-Dindo Class ≥1 complications (26% vs 16%; p = 0.09), complete response (90% vs 89%; p = 0.9), and overall-survival (3 vs 1.9 yrs.; p = 0.1). Neither modality was associated with a change in renal function at 12-months. CONCLUSION: For patients undergoing thermal ablation for cT1a RCC, CRA and MWA ablation have similar efficacy. MWA was associated with fewer probes and shorter procedure time. A lower incidence of any-size hematoma was observed with MWA; however, sample size and operator preference for CRA for slightly more centrally located lesions confound this observation and limit it as descriptive and hypothesis generating. Neither modality differed in complete response rates, overall-survival, nor reduction in renal function.

articles.title: Editorial for "Predicting Signal Intensity Profiles for Various MRI Contrast Agent Injection Strategies: Including Measurement of Relaxivities in Oxygenated Whole Human Blood for Gadopiclenol, Gadoterate Meglumine, and Gadoteridol".
Contrast-Enhanced Ultrasound for Target Localization Before Ultrasound-Guided Local Injection in Cesarean Scar Pregnancy.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVES: To evaluate the role of contrast-enhanced ultrasound (CEUS) in preprocedural target localization for cesarean scar pregnancy (CSP) and to assess the outcomes of ultrasound-guided local injection. METHODS: This retrospective study included 31 patients with CSP who underwent CEUS prior to ultrasound-guided local injection. CEUS was used to identify the hypervascular implantation site. Methotrexate (MTX) (50 mg) was administered locally into the gestational sac, followed by targeted injection toward the implantation site. Serum β-human chorionic gonadotropin (β-hCG) levels and ultrasound findings were monitored during follow-up. Initial treatment success was defined as a satisfactory decline in β-hCG levels after a single injection without additional MTX. RESULTS: CEUS demonstrated earlier enhancement and higher peak intensity at the implantation site than in the surrounding tissues (all p < .001). The hypervascular implantation region delineated by CEUS was significantly larger than that detected by color Doppler imaging (p < .001). Initial treatment success was achieved in 26 of 31 patients (83.87%). The mean time to β-hCG resolution after tissue removal was 21.78 ± 6.96 days. A major complication occurred in 1 patient (3.23%), who required surgical intervention due to severe bleeding. CONCLUSIONS: CEUS improves visualization of the hypervascular implantation site and may facilitate target localization before ultrasound-guided local injection. This approach appears feasible and relatively safe for the management of selected CSP patients.

articles.title: Missed abdominal injuries on initial trauma CT: pitfalls, mimickers and practical pearls.
articles.abstract: Missed and misinterpreted injuries on the initial trauma CT remain a major source of delayed diagnosis and preventable morbidity. This pictorial essay illustrates, with cases from our department, the abdominal injuries most often overlooked: bowel and mesenteric injury, diaphragmatic rupture, hepatic and splenic vascular injury, renal vascular injury, pancreatic injury and bladder rupture. For each, we show the subtle direct and indirect CT signs, the mimickers that lead to over- or under-calling (including unidentified bright objects of the spleen), and the roles of multiphasic CT, multiplanar reformats, dual-energy CT, MRCP and CT cystography. We close with a practical search strategy and a low threshold for repeat imaging when the clinical course is discordant with the first scan.
